proposition: Ibn Turka wrote twice to Sayyid Amīr Niẓām al-Dīn Aḥmad Ṣāʿidī (presumed): once asking him to look into the position of Sharaf al-Dīn Yaʿqūb and a group of Sufis (letter 6), once sending an introductory treatise on the science of letters (letter 15, ca. 817/1414 Shiraz), probably the R. Ḥurūf or possibly the R. Anjām.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Niẓām al-Dīn Aḥmad Ṣāʿidī (presumed)
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
mediation.note: Identity of the addressee and of the treatise are MK's presumptions
